liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Cat Sunflower** (2 reviews): Phil's bass playing in this song is the reviewer's only highlight; China Cat into Rider is singled out as pretty nice [15][16]
- **He's Gone** (2 reviews): Reviewer hears the coda as addressed to Garcia's addiction; The ending of He's Gone is described as wild [11][17]
- **Eyes Of The World** (2 reviews): Eyes is well played and a highlight, along with Spoonful; Reviewer enjoys the Eyes and the China Cat into Rider segment [17][19]
- **C. C. Rider** (1 review): Reviewer says Iko Iko and especially CC Rider merit a second listen [17]
- **Baby What You Want Me To Do** (1 other source): Last played previously on 12-31-82 [4]
- **Aiko Aiko** (1 review): Reviewer finds the Aiko into CC Rider pairing a pretty nice version [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **Baby What You Want Me To Do**: back after 138 archived shows (780 days); rare: 5 archived performances [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1985-02-18.170269.mtx.miksis.flac1648** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 144 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd85-02-18.sbd.willy.7588.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 142 min; rated 2.95/5 by 19 [2]. Said about its sound: Soundboard tape runs a little fast and needs speed correction; Pitch on the tape is slightly fast; Looks Like Rain does not appear on the soundboard tape, reportedly because it was so bad [10][11][13][16][19]
- **gd1985-02-18.170268.sbd.miksis.flac1648**: soundboard; 20 songs; 143 min [3]
- **gd1985-02-18.aud.mccue.82843.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 20 songs; 144 min; rated 1.5/5 by 2 [4]

## Around the show

- Fans spent hours before the show around Lake Merritt in fine weather, browsing vendors' wares near the venue [9]
- First show after Garcia's arrest in Golden Gate park; crowd excited to see him in a red t-shirt [9]
- Garcia sang with emotion and defiance, and the audience fed off it and returned the energy [9]
- Garcia seems newly off heroin; band is joyful about having him back, though they stumble a few times [11]
- Weir has serious vocal trouble, sounding as if he lost his voice [12]
- Reviewer hears weak vocals, low energy and many mistakes throughout [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1985-02-18.170269.mtx.miksis.flac1648**: transferred by Created by Brian Miksis February 15, 2025; source: SBD/AUD Matrix: Final Cut Pro (16b/48k) > Izotope RX Advanced > Peak Pro > xAct > FLAC/16 [1]. Also: Matrix of Charlie Miller's soundboard and Mark McCue's audience source, with pitch correction, hum removal and channel swaps on most songs [1]
- **gd85-02-18.sbd.willy.7588.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>CM>DAT>SoundForge>CD [2]. Also: Soundboard DAT from Charlie Miller, passed via John Spaventa, transferred through SoundForge to CD, seeded by Willy [2]
- **gd1985-02-18.170268.sbd.miksis.flac1648**: transferred by Matrix by Brian Miksis; source: Soundboard Source (shnid=7588): Cassette Master -> DAT - > SoundForge -> CD First circulated February 15, 2002 [3]. Also: Soundboard source tape from Charlie Miller, remastered with hum, dropouts and clicks fixed and pitch corrected; Mark McCue's audience recording, transferred by Alex Ford, supplies a tape flip patch [3]
- **gd1985-02-18.aud.mccue.82843.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Mark McCue; transferred by Alex Ford; source: MAC; Sennheiser 421s > Sony TC-MD5 > Maxell MX90s [4]. Also: Audience master cassettes from Mark McCue, transferred by Alex Ford in February 2007 [4]
